title: Regional pooling hides local P02 tracer mismatch with steady transport in 2013 and 2022 under fixed source assumptions
abstract: We test whether regional tracer fits to steady transport also fit local water columns. We use P02 CFC-12 and SF6 at 28-32 N on density 26.3-26.7 in 2013 and 2022. Linear programs test all nonnegative age spectra under fixed source histories, full source saturation and sample-based solubility. All 15 regional means fit unchanged spectra within 5 percent tracer error. Yet 55 of 124 local longitude-bin and density tests do not. Each occupation alone fits exactly. Wider bins retain the contrast: 38 of 92 local tests fail at 5 percent. The mean minimum changed spectral weight is only 1.07 percent in the main test, and only four local tests fail at 10 percent error. Eight of 15 region-density sets cannot fit every bin with shared tracer offsets below 5 percent plus independent 5 percent residuals. Strict interpolation removes most western and central coverage. Regional compatibility thus does not establish local steady transport, while the tracer data still permit small spectrum changes. Source changes, sparse bottle spacing, different station coverage and two occupations limit process inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Regional averaging hides local tracer mismatch, but the minimum required change of age-spectrum weight is small at 5 percent tolerance.
